A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from DVRF to DRFS. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-editing experiments, PIE benchmark results, trajectory measurements, ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and adds category-level comparisons and computational-resource measurements.

M1.justification: The residual objective, shifted latent, approximate gradient and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure, including the implemented shift c_t approximately equal to t(1-t). DVRF becomes DRFS; the new stability analysis explains an existing design rather than introducing another method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate on the 700-image PIE benchmark and the additional image collection, including the 340-image evaluation in Figure S5. The new pose/style breakdown and instruction-editor comparisons reuse PIE. Removing the FLUX experiment changes model configurations, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DNAEdit comparisons using FLUX and SD3.5. Appendix C.5 newly compares against InstructPix2Pix and MagicBrush, substantially broadening comparison scope to trained instruction-driven editors. V1's separate comparison of DVRF running on FLUX is removed, although its baseline methods remain elsewhere.

E3.justification: V3 adds category-specific PIE evaluation and NFE/peak-VRAM measurements alongside timing. It removes the reported FLUX configuration with 24 optimization steps. The retained SD3/SD3.5 experiments keep their optimization steps, guidance settings, datasets and editing-quality metrics.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a focused analysis of object-pose and image-style edits, comparing alignment and preservation against FlowEdit. Appendix B.3 expands computational-cost analysis. Existing shift, scheduler, batch-size and optimizer ablations, gradient visualizations and failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: V3 Table S1 newly reports mean and standard deviation across 700 images for runtime and peak VRAM. V1 provided mean runtimes only. Figure 3 already reported mean and standard deviation in both versions; no increase in repeated runs or seeds is established.

E6.justification: The reported evidence expands through DNAEdit, instruction-editor, pose/style and resource-result entries, while the DVRF-FLUX results disappear. Existing main and ablation scores remain unchanged. New results include pose-edit LPIPS of 91.4 for DRFS versus 102.6 for FlowEdit. Reported mean runtimes change from 7.4 to 7.3 seconds for the proposed method and 5.1 to 4.9 for FlowEdit, without establishing reruns or a methodological speedup.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.4 introduces optimization-error propagation, the amplification factor A_t, a Lipschitz assumption and a velocity-mismatch bound to motivate shift behavior at both endpoints. This materially extends the retained DDS/FlowEdit/DDIB connections. Equation 3 corrects the DDS source terms, but Appendix C.1 introduces an erroneous equality when splitting the gradient in Equation S4.

C1.justification: The inversion-free editing and DDS/FlowEdit unification claims remain. V3 explicitly claims stability-driven shift-design criteria and extends its named superiority comparisons to DNAEdit. The contribution list sharpens the existing residual-subtraction and trajectory-correction claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds an explicit error-reinjection explanation for early large shifts and interprets DDS/FlowEdit shift choices as suboptimal. It removes the FLUX-specific discussion of guidance-distillation constraints. The general rectified-flow limitation and failures involving large structural changes remain.

D1.justification: The advertised code location changes from the personal DVRF repository to the laboratory's DRFS repository. V3 documents NFE and peak-memory figures but removes FLUX-specific guidance, step-count and learning-rate instructions. Existing hardware, SD3/SD3.5 settings and dataset-generation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds FIVE, DNAEdit and SplitFlow citations, discussing direct noise alignment and SplitFlow's additional LLM/computation requirements. It replaces the GODIVA citation used for CLIP with Radford et al. The principal positioning relative to DDS, RFDS and FlowEdit remains.

P1.justification: V3 renames the method and title, rewrites the contribution list and selected explanatory paragraphs, and streamlines appendix organization. Duplicate qualitative-results and broader-impact sections are removed, and some FlowEdit explanation is consolidated. Most prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main paper and appendices switch from single-column to two-column layout, extensively relocating and resizing displays; Figure 1 moves to the opening page. Table 1 is regrouped and highlighted. New efficiency, category and instruction-comparison tables replace or supplement existing displays, while the FLUX table is removed. Most qualitative images and plotted findings are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 makes comparative and efficiency claims easier to assess through additional relevant baselines, difficult-category results and resource variability. Appendix B.4 also supplies an explicit mathematical rationale for the existing shift schedule. These are limited gains: core performance is unchanged, FLUX validation and its caveat are removed, and Equation S4 introduces a local mathematical error.
